info.name: Django Mindoff Showcase
info.description:
Every endpoint in the django-mindoff example repo, ready to run.

Quick start:
1. Start the server: `python manage.py runserver`
2. Import this collection into Postman.
3. The `base_url` collection variable defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000 — change it once and every request follows.

Requests are grouped by app: Shop (managed APIs, responses, validation, versioning), Catalog (bulk data + the benchmark), and Jobs (optional queue mode).

item.name: Shop
item.description: Managed APIs: response envelopes, payload validation, and same-route versioning (v1 vs v2).

request.description: The smallest possible managed API. Returns a static profile wrapped in the standard mo_response_kit envelope (code/category/message/data).

Validates the payload against the API's schema, creates the order, and returns a compact v1 confirmation. Try removing a field or sending a string for `quantity` to see the structured validation error.
Same route and same payload as v1, but the v2 handler returns a richer response body. Shows how APIVersionRouter serves multiple versions side by side.

item.name: Catalog
item.description: Bulk data workflows powered by mo_crud_kit + Polars, plus the headline create/read/update benchmark.

request.description: Row-level bulk validation. The second row is intentionally invalid (empty sku, negative price): it is rejected with a reason while the valid row is imported. The response includes a standard-vs-mindoff timing comparison for the valid rows.

Reads the full product table through mo_crud_kit into a Polars frame, then aggregates (totals, average price, per-category breakdown) with no Python row loop. Run Import Products first so there is data to report on.

Runs the create / read / update benchmark across each requested row count and writes deliverables under output/: one CSV (catalog_benchmark_values.csv) and one time+memory chart per operation (catalog_benchmark_create.png, _read.png, _update.png). Returned paths are in data.exports.

This can run for a while at large counts — DRF's serializer update path is the slow one. The committed charts in benchmarks/ were generated with row_count [10000, 50000, 100000]. Use bigger counts (and Postgres/MySQL) for the most meaningful comparison.

item.name: Jobs
item.description: Optional queue-mode endpoint. Requires Redis running and a Dramatiq worker; the rest of the repo works without either.

request.description: Submits an inventory report job. Because the API sets process_mode = "queue", Mindoff enqueues the work and returns a task handle with progress steps instead of running inline. Needs `redis-server` and `dramatiq django_mindoff.queue_worker` running.
